frictions.title: Availability grid time slots lack accessible labels and dates
frictions.description: When navigating the event availability grid with VoiceOver, time slot elements announce only generic times or 'group' without conveying column dates, slot duration, or selection state, preventing non-visual scheduling (WCAG 1.3.1, 4.1.2).

interventions.description: Expose accessible names, dates, times, and selection states on the availability grid slots for screen readers.

The availability grid in #YouGridSlots is built from generic div elements with no grid/row/cell (or button) roles, no accessible names, and no exposed selection state. While navigating slots with VoiceOver, the user heard only bare time strings such as '9:00 AM' or the word 'group', with no indication of which date column the slot belongs to, the slot's duration, or whether the slot is currently marked as available. Activations with VO-Space produced no state announcement either. A screen reader user therefore cannot determine the coordinates of the cell they are on, cannot confirm that a toggle succeeded, and cannot complete availability entry non-visually.
interventions.mitigation: Give each interactive slot an accessible name that includes the full date and time range, and expose its role and state programmatically — for example role="button" with tabindex="0" and aria-pressed reflecting availability, or a proper grid structure (role="grid"/"row"/"gridcell" with column headers associated to the date columns) so the date and time are conveyed through relationships. Update the exposed state whenever a slot is toggled, and announce the resulting change (e.g., via an aria-live status region) so confirmation is available without sight.

frictions.title: Unlabeled link in VoiceOver rotor links menu
frictions.description: When navigating page links via the VoiceOver rotor, an anchor element lacking accessible text is announced simply as 'link', concealing its destination and purpose from non-visual screen reader users (WCAG 2.4.4, 4.1.2).

interventions.description: Add an accessible label to the unlabeled link on the page.

An anchor element on the page has no text content or accessible name. When the user opened the VoiceOver rotor Links menu, this entry was announced only as 'link' (observed on repeated visits to the menu), so its destination and purpose are not discoverable. Screen reader users scanning the link list cannot tell whether the link is relevant and may have to activate it blindly to find out.
interventions.mitigation: Provide an accessible name for the anchor: add visible link text, or if the link is intentionally icon-only/graphical, supply alt text on the contained image or an aria-label describing the destination or purpose. Ensure the name reflects where the link goes rather than a generic string.

frictions.title: Carousel buttons share ambiguous 'Visit linked content' accessible name
frictions.description: Interactive gallery carousel buttons use a generic aria-label of 'Visit linked content', overriding specific child image alt attributes and announcing identical ambiguous names to VoiceOver (WCAG 2.4.6, 4.1.2).

interventions.description: Replace generic 'Visit linked content' labels on carousel buttons with specific item descriptions.

The interactive items in the homepage gallery carousel each carry a hard-coded aria-label of 'Visit linked content' on the container element. Because that aria-label overrides the accessible name that would otherwise be derived from the child image's alt text (e.g. 'Little Leaders Characters', 'Little Leaders Videos'), VoiceOver announced an identical, non-descriptive name for all carousel items — observed 16 times across the session, including 5 consecutive repetitions while the user navigated back through the controls. A screen reader user cannot tell the items apart, cannot predict where any item leads, and must activate items by trial and error or rely on surrounding visual context that is not exposed non-visually.
interventions.mitigation: Give each carousel item a unique, meaningful accessible name that reflects its destination or content instead of the shared 'Visit linked content' string. For the observed markup, either remove the generic aria-label from the `.eapp-photo-gallery-item-data-component` container so the descriptive `alt` text on the child `.eapp-photo-gallery-item-data-image` supplies the name, or set the container's aria-label to that same specific text (e.g. aria-label="Little Leaders Characters"). If the gallery is generated by a third-party widget, configure per-item link titles/alt text in the widget settings, or apply the correction idempotently after render and re-apply when the carousel updates its DOM. Also verify the element's exposed role matches its behaviour (link vs. button) so the announcement is consistent with what activation actually does.

ablation.source_capture: blind - Ambiguous elements - Little Leaders - pathway 1/web/page_0002_www.littleleaders.com

blind.description: The Elfsight photo-gallery carousel exposes each slide as a generic `div role="button" aria-label="Visit linked content"` (repeated many times because Swiper duplicates slides), so a screen-reader user hears a dozen identical, purpose-less controls with no idea of the destination.

The Elfsight previous/next controls are `div role="button" aria-label="Previous"/"Next"` with no `tabindex`, so they are not focusable and a keyboard/screen-reader user cannot move through that gallery at all.

Both the desktop and mobile header markup (plus the overlay menu) are present in the DOM, so the Shop/Books/Playground/About links, the "Login" link and the "0 items in cart" link are announced two to three times, and the two `background-pause-button` pairs expose both "Pause Background" and "Play Background" simultaneously, creating duplicated, contradictory controls.
The menu toggle button computes the name "Open Menu Close Menu" (both spans read) and carries no `aria-expanded`, so its purpose and open/closed state are not conveyed.

Decorative scrolling marquee phrases are marked up as multiple `<h1>` elements ("Motor Skill Development", "•", "Multi-Lingual Content") and "Why Little Leaders?" is another h1, so heading navigation returns meaningless, duplicated headings instead of a real page structure.

low_vision.description: The marquee block scrolls its heading text continuously along an SVG path with no pause/stop control, making the text impossible to read at magnification.

Two auto-rotating carousels (the Elfsight swiper gallery and the `user-items-list-carousel` with its "Item 1 of 8" live region) change content on their own, so magnified users lose the item they were reading.

Long white bold testimonial text (`sqsrte-text-color--white`) sits directly over a photographic section background (`image-asset.jpg`) with only a translucent overlay, so contrast varies and can fall below 4.5:1.

Headings use Squarespace viewport-scaled text (`sqsrte-scaled-text-container`) and fluid image blocks, so text size is tied to container width rather than user text settings and can clip or fail to enlarge when zoomed/resized.

The transparent sticky header (`tweak-transparent-header`, `tweak-fixed-header-style-scroll-back`) overlays page content and consumes a large share of the viewport at high zoom, obscuring content beneath it.

dhh.description: The embedded Vimeo videos ("Little Leaders Classics Video Series (Official Trailer)" and "Why Little Leaders?") are presented with no indication of captions, so their narration, music and dialogue are inaccessible.

No transcript or text alternative accompanies either video block — the only adjacent text is the credit "A message from our founder, Bradley Silvius" — so the spoken content of the founder's message is unavailable.

motor.description: The Elfsight gallery relies on Swiper drag/swipe plus `div role="button"` arrows that are not in the tab order, leaving no keyboard or single-pointer alternative for browsing its slides.
The marquee's clickable hitbox path and the auto-advancing carousels move continuously, forcing users to hit a moving target with no way to stop the motion first.

Interactive icons are small and thin — the cart icon, the hairline SVG carousel arrows (`user-items-list-carousel__arrow-icon`, 24×14 mobile arrows) and the Elfsight 16×16 arrow icons — making accurate pointer activation difficult.
Footer links are packed inline with only whitespace between them (`Privacy Policy Terms and Conditions`), so adjacent targets are effectively touching and easy to mis-click.

Because both desktop and mobile header blocks plus the overlay menu are all in the DOM, keyboard users must tab through triplicated nav links, "Login" (an inert `href="#"` link) and cart links before reaching content, greatly increasing keystrokes and dead-end activations.

friction_results.note: Audit barrier 0 identifies the 'Visit linked content' generic aria-label issue for the gallery/category items.

frictions.description: Interactive gallery items use a static aria-label of 'Visit linked content' on container divs, overriding specific image alt attributes. VoiceOver announces every carousel button identically as 'Visit linked content button', preventing screen reader users from distinguishing distinct targets (WCAG 2.4.4, WCAG 4.1.2).

interventions.description: Replace generic carousel button labels with descriptive item names.

Interactive gallery/carousel items on the home page are container divs carrying a static aria-label of 'Visit linked content'. Because this label is applied on the container, it overrides the more specific alt text of the enclosed images, so VoiceOver announces every item as 'Visit linked content button'. In the observed session the user reviewed these items via the VoiceOver Rotor and could not distinguish one target from another; they activated one with VO+Space and navigated to the Shop page without knowing in advance where the control led. Non-visual users therefore cannot choose among gallery targets, and must rely on trial-and-error navigation and back-tracking.
interventions.mitigation: Give each interactive gallery item a unique, descriptive accessible name instead of a shared static string. For elements matching the gallery item container pattern (e.g. .eapp-photo-gallery-item-data-component with aria-label='Visit linked content'), derive the name from the item's existing descriptive content — such as the enclosed image's alt text or the item's title/caption — or remove the container aria-label so the inner image alt text is exposed. Ensure duplicated or dynamically cloned slides receive the same distinct names, and verify the resulting announcement for each item with VoiceOver and in the accessibility tree.

frictions.title: Visual Click CAPTCHA challenge is inaccessible to VoiceOver screen reader
frictions.description: The demo visual CAPTCHA requires clicking specific image coordinates but provides no audio alternative or accessible description. Activating the image via VoiceOver produces no functional interaction or state feedback.

interventions.description: The click CAPTCHA challenge requires the user to identify and click specific coordinates within an image. Under VoiceOver, the image conveyed no description of the challenge content or target locations, and repeated VO+Space activations (observed four times in quick succession) produced no announced result, no selection of a coordinate, and no state change feedback. A nonvisual keyboard user therefore has no way to perceive what must be clicked, no keyboard-operable means of making a selection, and no confirmation of whether an activation registered, which blocks completion of the challenge and any flow gated behind it.
interventions.mitigation: Provide a non-visual alternative path for the same security check on the same page (for example an audio challenge, a text-based or logic challenge, or a mechanism that does not depend on recognizing and clicking image content), and make that alternative reachable and announced in the reading order near the visual challenge. For the visual widget itself, expose the challenge instructions as programmatically associated text rather than only inside the image, give the interactive element an accurate accessible name and role so it is not presented as an inert image, provide a keyboard-operable way to choose targets (for example labelled focusable target regions or a grid of named choices instead of raw coordinate clicking), and announce selection and pass/fail results through a live region so state changes are perceivable without sight.

blind.description: The demo's only challenge is a bitmap CAPTCHA image (`img alt="clickcaptcha example"` inside `_widget_s7q0j_5`) that must be solved by clicking coordinates, with no audio, text or other non-visual alternative, so a screen-reader user cannot complete the form at all.

The CAPTCHA image's alt text ("clickcaptcha example") and the form provide no instruction about what must be clicked and no labelled clickable targets, leaving the blind user with no way to know the task or supply an answer.
The form (`_widgetForm_151cx_26`) has only "Check" and "Reset" buttons and no live region or status container, so success/failure feedback after submission is never announced.

Header dropdown triggers ("Captcha solver", "Scrapers", "Resources") are bare `<button>` elements with no aria-haspopup/aria-expanded, while their large panels' link text is still exposed in the accessible name/tree, so state is unknown and huge hidden menus are read out of context.

There is no skip link and headings jump from the single `h1` ("Click captcha demo") straight to `h3` ("How to solve ClickCaptcha"), so screen-reader users must traverse the entire mega-menu and cannot navigate by a coherent heading outline.

low_vision.description: The CAPTCHA is a fixed 200×230 raster image containing the text/objects to identify, so magnifying it pixelates the content and low-vision users cannot reliably see or click the required elements.

interventions.description: Add heading ARIA semantics to Craigslist category section headers.

The category section titles on the Craigslist area homepage (community, housing, jobs, for sale) look like section headings visually, but they are implemented as plain <a> elements with no <h1>-<h6> markup and no role="heading". frictions.description: Under high macOS Zoom magnification, logical flight attributes (times, airlines, stops) and price details cannot fit within a single viewport, forcing repetitive horizontal panning across wide result rows to correlate flight details with prices (WCAG 1.4.10).

interventions.description: Use Safari browser zoom (Command-Minus ⌘-) to adjust the web page scale so that full flight rows reflow and fit within the magnified viewport.

The "Loading results" progressbars (`role="progressbar" aria-label="Loading results" aria-hidden="true"`) are hidden from AT, so the asynchronous fetching and arrival of the 23 flight results is not announced.

The ticket-type and cabin-class widgets are custom comboboxes whose `aria-controls` points at an empty `aria-hidden="true"` listbox (ids i9 / i22) while the real options live in a separate `ul`, and the combobox itself carries `aria-live="polite"`, producing wrong or duplicated announcements of the available/selected values.

Primary navigation is built from `<button ... role="link">` items (Explore, Flights, Hotels) and duplicated in the drawer as `div role="link" tabindex="0"` with labels like "Selected Tab: Flights", giving conflicting role/state semantics and a second, redundant navigation set to screen-reader users.

low_vision.description: The viewport meta sets `maximum-scale=1.0, user-scalable=no`, preventing pinch/browser zoom of the flight search UI on touch devices.
The date-picker dialog renders several full month grids (July–October…) side by side in a fixed-width scrolling panel, forcing both horizontal and vertical scrolling once magnified.

Icon-only controls (swap origin/destination, add multiple airports, change appearance, calendar month chevrons) convey their purpose only through hover-triggered tooltips (`EY8ABd-OWXEXe-TAWMXe`, `aria-hidden="true"` until hover) that a magnifier user may never see or that disappear on pointer movement.

Calendar state such as the chosen departure day is signalled only by background/color styling classes (e.g. `Ic3tg NXzzqb g7lVZ` on August 18), with no visible non-color indicator, making the selection hard to spot when zoomed or in low contrast.

Key controls use very small glyphs and dense text (16–18px SVG stepper and remove icons, single-letter weekday headers, tiny "Aged 2-11" secondary labels), which pixelate/clip badly under screen magnification.

motor.description: Selecting travel dates requires hitting tiny, tightly packed day cells in the month grids (`div.WhDFk` gridcells), whose inner activatable `role="button"` is `tabindex="-1"`, so imprecise pointer users have no reliably large target or simple tab-stop alternative.

The calendar's month/step chevron buttons are `tabindex="-1" aria-hidden="true"` inside containers wired to `mousedown`/hover handlers, so they are effectively pointer-hover-only with no keyboard-operable equivalent.

Passenger counts must be set by repeatedly clicking 16px `+`/`−` icon buttons ("Add adult", "Remove infant on lap") that sit immediately next to each other, demanding repeated precise clicks with no direct numeric entry.

Origin/destination chips place a small `role="button"` "Remove" control (16px X icon) inside the selected `role="option"` item, so a slightly off-target click deletes the chosen city instead of selecting it.

frictions.title: Small popup overlay close button target size
frictions.description: The close button on the promotional discount popup overlay is small and difficult to target, causing multiple missed clicks and extra panning effort while using screen magnification.

interventions.description: Enlarge the close button touch target area on the popup overlay.

The close (dismiss) control on the promotional discount pop-up overlay presents a very small clickable area. While using macOS full-screen Zoom, the user had to pan the magnified viewport to locate the control and then produced multiple missed clicks (observed roughly 18.8s-21.3s) before the overlay was finally dismissed around 0:28. Because the overlay blocks interaction with the underlying store content, a hard-to-hit dismiss target directly delays or blocks the user's primary task, and the cost is amplified for anyone with reduced pointer precision or a magnified viewport where only a fraction of the page is visible at a time.
interventions.mitigation: Increase the effective hit area of the pop-up's close control to at least 44x44 CSS pixels (e.g., by adding padding or an enlarged pseudo-element/inline-block wrapper around the icon rather than only scaling the glyph), and ensure adjacent targets remain unobstructed. Give the control a clearly visible hover and keyboard focus indicator so its boundaries are discoverable under magnification, and confirm it exposes an accessible name such as "Close". Additionally consider positioning the dismiss control predictably relative to the dialog content and supporting Escape-key dismissal so the pop-up can be closed without precise pointer targeting.

blind.description: The header wishlist control (`<a href="/pages/wishlist" class="header_wishlist_icon">` containing only decorative heart SVGs) exposes no accessible name — it appears in the accessibility tree as a link with name null, so screen-reader users cannot tell what it does.

The mobile navigation drawer's expandable sections are non-focusable `<h3 class="sub-menu accordion__toggle">` elements and the top-level "WOMEN"/"MEN" buttons carry no aria-expanded, so screen-reader users get no role or state information and cannot open the sub-category lists.

The country switcher and Help popovers use `role="listbox"` wrapping `<button>` elements that each contain an `<a>` link, an invalid nesting of interactive elements that makes market/help options misannounced and unreliable to activate with a screen reader.

The "STAY IN THE LOOP" newsletter form's required email input has no label or accessible name (tree shows required textbox with name "") alongside several other unnamed inputs, so blind users cannot know what to enter.

Quick-add size pickers on every product card use a `<fieldset class="variant-picker__option">` with no legend and labels reading only "XS…XXL", and each card wraps them in a `role="region" aria-live="polite"` container, giving context-free, repeatedly announced controls that can't be tied to a product or size purpose.

low_vision.description: The viewport meta declares `minimum-scale=1.0, maximum-scale=1.0`, disabling pinch-zoom so magnification users cannot scale this page's small product text and swatches on mobile.

Product-card purchasing controls (`product-card__quick-buy`, inline size buttons) and the desktop mega menus (`details is="mega-menu-disclosure" trigger="hover"`) only appear on hover, so at high magnification the content pops in and out of the visible viewport and is easily lost.

The announcement bar (`announcement-bar` cycling four promo messages with is="prev-button"/"next-button") and the hero `slideshow-carousel` auto-advance with no visible pause/stop control, moving offers away before a magnified reader finishes them.

Marketing text is placed directly over full-bleed photographs using theme-color classes (e.g. slideshow "Comfort-first Activewear" / "Engage is designed to move when you do" in `.text-custom`, and mega-menu labels "leggings guide"/"golf" over images), risking insufficient text-to-background contrast.

A sticky, scroll-reacting header (`store-header ... hide-on-scroll="100" sticky`) plus horizontally scrolling product carousels (`scroll-carousel ... is-scrollable`) consume viewport height and force two-directional panning when the page is enlarged.

motor.description: Many primary controls are far below minimum target size — 17×17px wishlist heart icons on each product card, 10×7 and 5×8 chevron icons in the localisation/announcement/section controls, and tightly spaced `block-swatch` size labels — making accurate pointing very hard.

Add-to-cart affordances and desktop navigation are hover-dependent (`product-card__quick-buy` revealed on hover; `<details is="mega-menu-disclosure" trigger="hover">`), requiring sustained, steady pointer hold over large menu areas to keep them open.

Product rows and the announcement bar are swipe/drag-scroll regions (`scroll-carousel ... is-scrollable`, `<announcement-bar swipeable>`), so browsing items depends on a dragging gesture whose only alternatives are the tiny prev/next chevron buttons.

The announcement bar and hero slideshow rotate automatically with no pause control, so links such as "Free US Shipping On Orders Over $65" can move out from under a slow-moving pointer before activation.

Mobile-drawer sub-menu expanders are plain `<h3 class="accordion__toggle">` headings rather than buttons, so keyboard-only users cannot focus or activate them to reach category, size and colour links.

frictions.title: Filter search result update outside magnified viewport
frictions.description: Activating sidebar filters updates the result count and product grid outside the user's magnified area, forcing extensive manual panning across the screen to locate updated content.

interventions.description: On the search results page, activating a sidebar filter checkbox (e.g. seller, price range, 'Outdoor' usage) asynchronously updates the result count and the product grid, which are laid out horizontally distant from the filter controls. Under screen magnification only a small portion of the page is visible, so the update happens entirely outside the user's visible viewport and provides no perceivable feedback at the point of interaction. This was observed three times in the session: after each filter activation the user had to perform a full-screen pan traversal to find the updated count and listing, adding significant effort and uncertainty about whether the filter had applied at all.
interventions.mitigation: Announce and surface filter results where the interaction happens: expose the updated result count via a live region (e.g. role="status"/aria-live="polite") so assistive technology and magnifier-aware users get immediate feedback, and additionally render a visible, near-the-control indicator of the applied filter and resulting count (for example an inline count next to each filter option or a sticky 'N results' summary adjacent to the filter panel). Optionally move programmatic focus to the results heading after the grid updates so magnified views follow the change, and keep the applied-filter chips within or immediately adjacent to the filter region rather than only at the top of the grid.

frictions.title: Navigation menu links fail contrast against slideshow background
frictions.description: Light cyan text used for primary navigation links ('food & drinks', 'menu guide', 'catering') rendered over varied background photos provides insufficient visual contrast (WCAG 1.4.3), forcing the user to repeatedly pan and magnify the viewport to read them.

interventions.description: Add a semi-transparent dark backdrop behind navigation links to ensure high contrast and legibility.

Primary navigation links ('food & drinks', 'menu guide', 'catering') are drawn in light cyan text on top of varied photographic backgrounds that change as the hero slideshow advances. Because no consistent backing layer separates the text from the imagery, the text-to-background contrast is unpredictable and insufficient on lighter or busy frames. Observed consequence: the person had to keep macOS Zoom active and pan the magnified viewport horizontally across the menu multiple times to resolve the link labels, which slows down and complicates a basic navigation task and can leave link text effectively unreadable on some slides.
interventions.mitigation: Give the navigation text a background it controls rather than relying on the underlying photo. For example, apply a solid or semi-transparent dark backdrop (with adequate padding) behind the link text in the navigation container, or use a fixed dark bar/scrim across the nav region, and pair it with a light text colour so the computed contrast ratio meets at least 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text) against that backdrop on every slide. Verify the ratio against the darkest and lightest slideshow frames rather than a single image. Keep hover and focus states visually distinct from the resting state and ensure those states also meet the contrast requirement, so the currently targeted link remains identifiable when magnified.

frictions.description: Magnified panning near a hover popup's boundary dismisses it before the user can finish reading its content.

frictions.title: Navigation header hover menus dismiss during magnified pointer travel
frictions.description: While using screen magnification, hovering navigation triggers like 'Medical Care' and 'Prime' opens transient flyouts. Panning across the magnified viewport causes the pointer to drift off narrow hover boundaries, prematurely dismissing the flyout and requiring repeated re-triggers.

interventions.description: Header navigation items such as 'Medical Care' and 'Prime' reveal additional content in a hover-triggered flyout. The flyout is dismissed as soon as the pointer leaves a narrow hover region around the trigger and panel, with no tolerance for small pointer excursions or gaps between the trigger and the panel. Under screen magnification only a fraction of the flyout is visible at once, so the user must pan the pointer to read the content; this panning repeatedly moved the pointer outside the hover region and closed the menu (observed at least three times), requiring the user to re-hover the trigger and restart reading. The consequence is that magnified users cannot reliably read or reach items inside these menus.
interventions.mitigation: Make the hover-revealed content persistent and forgiving: keep the flyout open while the pointer is anywhere over the trigger or the panel, include the intervening space (bridging area) in the hover region, and add a dismissal delay/hover-intent grace period so brief pointer excursions do not close it. Provide an explicit dismissal path that does not depend on pointer position (e.g. Esc key and/or a close affordance), and ensure the menus can also be opened and kept open via click/keyboard activation rather than hover alone. Verify the behaviour at high magnification levels where only part of the panel is on screen.

blind.description: The interactive seat map is a bare SVG of thousands of `<circle class="seat is-available">` elements with no roles, accessible names, or focusability, so a screen-reader user gets no information about, and cannot select, individual seats.

Ticket listings are marked up as a `role="menu"` with `role="menuitem"` rows (aria-haspopup="dialog") and the actual price/buy element is a `span` with `tabindex="-1"`, so listings are announced as menu commands, Tab reaches only one item, and the purchase control has no button semantics.

The min/max price filter inputs are given the invalid `role="text"` (`<input role="text" aria-label="Minimum price $53">`), stripping their textbox semantics so screen-reader users cannot discover or edit the price filter.

The date picker container is a `div role="menu" tabindex="0"` whose month navigation and every day button are `aria-hidden="true"` and disabled, so it focuses as a single element announced as one concatenated string ("Close CalendarGo back one monthAugust 2026…") with no usable date controls.

Page structure is unhelpful for AT navigation: two identical `

Henry Cho: The Empty Nest Tour

` elements, no `main` landmark, and the ticket list/map sections sit in unlabeled generic divs, making it hard to locate the buying area.

low_vision.description: The viewport meta declares `maximum-scale=1.0, user-scalable=no`, blocking pinch-zoom so magnification users cannot enlarge the dense ticket list, prices, or seat map.

Seat availability/filter state in the map is conveyed only through fill color of 40-unit dots (classes `is-available`/`is-filtered`) with no text, shape, or pattern cue, so low-vision users cannot tell available from unavailable seats.

blind.description: The cookie consent dialog that opens over the page exposes unresolved template tokens as content and accessible names (tab named "[#IABV2SETTINGS#]", "[#GPC_TOAST_TEXT#]", heading "[#BULK_CONSENT_TITLE#]"), a role="switch" input with no accessible name, and a tablist where every tab reports aria-selected="false", so a screen-reader user cannot tell what the consent controls are or which panel is active.

All submenu expand controls in the header and mobile navigation are announced as "Workspace.Header.ToggleSubmenu" (a raw localisation key repeated on Spaces, Locations, Why Workspace? and Meeting Rooms), giving no indication of what each button opens.

The mobile navigation trigger is a bare <span> labelled "Mobile menu toggle" with no button role or tabindex, so it is not announced or operable as a control and the mobile menu cannot be opened from the keyboard/screen reader.

There is no skip link or in-page landmark shortcut before the banner, breadcrumb and multi-level navigation, forcing screen-reader users to traverse dozens of repeated menu links before reaching the 150+ glossary headings in <main>.

Images carry non-informative alt text: the hero image alt embeds the file name ("...romain-vignes-53940-unsplash-banner") and a tracking pixel is exposed as an image named "dot image pixel", adding meaningless announcements.

low_vision.description: The consent dialog places its text and controls in nested internal scroll areas (CybotCookiebotScrollContainer/ScrollArea with fade overlays), so at high magnification the "Allow all"/"Deny" buttons and category text require two-dimensional scrolling inside a clipped panel.

The Necessary/Preferences/Statistics/Marketing consent controls are slider switches whose on/off state is conveyed only by the slider position and colour, with no visible text state, making the current consent choice hard to perceive when enlarged or with reduced colour perception.

Visible interface text includes unresolved placeholders and internal keys ("[#IABV2SETTINGS#]", "[#GPC_TOAST_TEXT#]", "Workspace.Header.ToggleSubmenu"), which magnified users must decode letter-by-letter without gaining any meaning.

A sticky header (body class "is-scrolled") plus persistently floating "Back to top" and "Open cookie settings widget" buttons overlay the content area, obscuring text and controls when the viewport is reduced by zoom.

The glossary presents over 150 consecutive h2 term sections in one continuous page with no A–Z index or in-page jump links, requiring extremely long panning/scrolling at magnification to locate a term.

dhh.description: The only direct contact routes offered in the header are a telephone number ("0204 638 0662") and a "Request a callback" button, i.e. voice-only channels, with no text-based equivalent surfaced on the page for users who cannot use the phone.

motor.description: Desktop header submenus in the "Secondary core dropdown links" navigation appear as hover/transient dropdown panels, requiring the user to hold the pointer steady over the trigger and traverse into the panel without losing it.
The mobile menu trigger is a non-focusable <span> ("Mobile menu toggle") with no keyboard-operable button semantics, leaving keyboard-only or switch users unable to open that navigation.

Numerous controls are small and tightly packed — the five footer social icon links, the chevron submenu toggle buttons sitting immediately beside their sibling link, breadcrumb links, and the thin consent slider switches — making accurate pointer activation difficult.

With no skip link and a page containing the full header/mega-menu, 150+ glossary sections and a large footer, dismissing the consent dialog and reaching content requires a very large number of sequential keyboard actions and scrolling, with only a "Back to top" button as a shortcut.

blind.description: The actual puzzle (four images plus the guess interface) is rendered inside the third-party Devvit web view (`devvit2-custom-post` / `devvit2-surface` with `entrypointUrl` to devvit.net) that exposes no accessible name, role or content in the accessibility tree, so a screen-reader user cannot perceive or play the game the page exists for.

The four puzzle photos are supplied only as raw JPEG URLs in the post's `developerData.images` payload with no text alternative or description, so the entire task ('find the word these 4 pictures share') is unavailable non-visually.

Landmarks pick up inline script text as their accessible names (banner/nav announced as "Open menu SML.load([\"8mAt_CUDml\"…]" and `main` as "SML.load([..."), so landmark navigation yields meaningless gibberish labels.

Heading structure is broken: the post title is an `h1` and the comment tree adds a second visually hidden `h1` "Comments Section", giving two top-level headings and no logical outline for jumping between post and discussion.

Each comment is a `details role="article" tabindex="0"` whose collapse affordance is an `aria-hidden` threadline `div` and whose spoiler hint uses a bare `shreddit-spoiler` element, so expanded/collapsed and hidden/revealed states are neither announced nor operable.

low_vision.description: The game is embedded in a fixed-size surface (`postStyles` height TALL / `heightPixels: 512`) that does not reflow, so magnifying the page clips or requires two-dimensional scrolling of the puzzle grid and answer keys.

Metadata that carries essential information (subreddit, `faceplate-timeago` timestamps, flair "Jul 22 | Puzzle 133", "Promoted", vote/score text) is rendered at 12px in the muted `text-neutral-content-weak` colour, which is too small and too low-contrast to read when enlarged or with reduced acuity.

The header (`reddit-header-large` with `fixed top-0` and full-width nav) stays pinned while scrolling, so at high magnification it covers a large share of the viewport and obscures the post and comment content.

Key labels and previews are delivered only through hover-triggered `rpl-tooltip` (trigger="hover focus-visible") and `faceplate-hovercard` (`mouse-only`, 500ms enter / 150ms leave), transient content that a magnifier user cannot reliably hover, enlarge or dismiss.

Primary controls are 16–20px icon-only glyphs with no visible text (overflow `…` buttons, share, chat, notifications, the 12px chip close icon), giving no perceivable boundaries or labels when magnified.

dhh.description: The promoted unit in the comment stream registers video events (`VIDEO_STARTED`, `VIDEO_PLAYED_WITH_SOUND`, `VIDEO_WATCHED_50/75/95`) yet no caption track or transcript is provided for that advertising media.
The embedded game web view supplies no textual transcript or caption mechanism for any audio feedback it plays, and the host page exposes no player or caption controls for it.

motor.description: Many actionable controls are 12–20px icon targets packed closely together (post and comment `Open user actions` overflow buttons, share, award, chat/notification icons, the 12px search-chip close icon), well under the 24×24 CSS px minimum and easy to mis-hit.

Comment threads collapse via a pointer-only `div.threadline-strip` that is `aria-hidden` and not focusable, so keyboard-only or switch users cannot collapse/expand threads in a 112-comment discussion.

Essential labels and previews appear only on hover with short dwell/leave timings (`rpl-tooltip`, `faceplate-hovercard mouse-only` with 500ms enter and 150ms leave), which users with tremor or imprecise pointing cannot trigger or keep open.

The interactive puzzle lives entirely inside the Devvit web view with no host-page keyboard affordance or alternative input path, so the game may be unreachable and unplayable without precise pointer input.

The comment composer's editable region uses a positive `tabindex="1"` (`div slot="rte" contenteditable role="textbox" tabindex="1"`), which pulls focus out of document order and makes sequential keyboard navigation of the page unpredictable.

blind.description: The message list is a custom grid whose rows, checkboxes and subject "links" are all removed from the tab order (tr tabindex="-1", div role="checkbox" tabindex="-1", div class="xS" role="link" with no tabindex), and the per-row action toolbar items (<li class="bqX brq"> etc. under ul role="toolbar") have no role, name or tabindex, so a screen-reader user cannot reach or identify archive/delete/snooze/mark-read for a message.

The whole banner is wrapped in an

so the level-1 heading is announced as a meaningless run-on string ("GmailSearchtabHelpTrainingSend feedback to GoogleUpgrade…Try Gemini"), and the page repeats identical hidden headings (three

Conversations

, two

Labels

), making heading navigation useless for orienting in the inbox.

Three near-identical mail toolbars (inbox, trash, spam variants) plus duplicated element ids used for naming (id="s" twice, id=":50" and id=":52" repeated in the tab panels) coexist in the DOM, so screen-reader users encounter multiple "Select", "Refresh", "More email options" and "inbox settings" controls with ambiguous or wrongly resolved accessible names.

Focusable controls are hidden from assistive technology, e.g. the Purchases label menu trigger <div class="pM aj0" tabindex="0" aria-haspopup="true" aria-hidden="true"> and the "More Add-ons" side-panel tab (role="tab" aria-hidden="true"), so keyboard focus lands on items the screen reader announces as nothing.

Several interactive items are generic elements without roles — the "inbox settings" spans (<span tabindex="0" class="aRq">) and the onboarding promo rows (<div class="OU" jsaction="click:OhaSLe">) — so they are announced as static text and their operability is not conveyed.

low_vision.description: Per-message actions (archive, delete, mark as read, snooze) only render when the row is hovered (ul class="bqY" revealed on row hover), so magnified users who cannot see the whole row lose these controls and have no persistent equivalent.

Nearly all commands are unlabeled 20 px icon glyphs drawn from sprites/transparent spacers (images/cleardot.gif for star, pagination "Newer"/"Older", toolbar div class="asf"/"ar9" backgrounds), which become indistinguishable when enlarged or when background images are overridden by a custom stylesheet.

Unread status is signalled visually only by bold/darker styling (class "zF"/"bqe"/"bq3" versus "yP") with no visible text or icon, so low-vision users cannot reliably tell the unread "Study task email" from read messages.

The inbox uses an 11-column grid table plus fixed left navigation, sticky toolbars and a right side panel (role="complementary" "Side panel"), forcing two-dimensional scrolling of the message list at high zoom.

Secondary information is rendered in small light-grey text (snippet spans class="y2", timestamps, "0% of 15 GB used", "Last account activity: 0 minutes ago", icons filled #5F6368), which is hard to read for users needing higher contrast.

motor.description: Opening or triaging a message requires precise mouse clicks because rows, cells, checkboxes and the subject "link" are excluded from the tab order (tabindex="-1" or no tabindex on div role="link" class="xS"), leaving no standard keyboard path to the messages.

The row action buttons only exist while the pointer hovers the row (ul class="bqY" toolbar and the hover-revealed label arrow div class="pM aj0"), so users must hold a hover and then hit a small icon without drifting off the row — an unreliable transient interaction.

Many essential targets are tiny and tightly packed: the star cell (span class="aXw" over a spacer gif), the row checkbox, the 20 px toolbar icons, the tab-visibility button (div class="aKj") and the "Newer"/"Older" pagination arrows, all adjacent within a dense row.

Menu and chip controls fire on pointer-down/mouse-down (e.g. jsaction="pointerdown:FEiYhc", "mousedown:UX7yZ", "mousedown:p8EH2c" on the search-refinement buttons and dropdowns), so a tremor or mis-press activates them with no chance to move off and abort.

Layered popup menus reached only through icon triggers ("Move to", "More email options", "Inbox section options", the label ▼ arrow) demand sustained fine-pointer traversal from trigger to menu item, with the label arrow being both hover-dependent and aria-hidden, offering no simpler alternative path.

frictions.description: In the filter panel, 'CLEAR ALL' sits adjacent to 'VIEW ITEMS'; an imprecise click aimed at applying filters lands on CLEAR ALL, silently discarding every selected filter with no confirmation or undo.

items.description: Separate CLEAR ALL from VIEW ITEMS, require confirmation before clearing active filters, and provide undo; both targets meet WCAG 2.5.8 target size.
